The lexicographic product puts a copy of the team in each department (the shaded groups, L and R in each): the teal edges copy H inside each copy, and because sales and ops are linked, four accent edges join every member of one team to every member of the other. The result is a complete graph on 4 nodes with 6 edges." width="100%"} The lexicographic product $G[H]$ replaces every node of this graph by a copy of `other`, and joins *every* node of one copy to every node of another copy whenever the two original nodes are adjacent. Formally, `(g, h)` and `(g', h')` are joined if `g`-`g'` is an edge, or if `g = g'` and `h`-`h'` is an edge of `other`. It is the natural model of a network of modules: departments (this graph) staffed by teams (`other`), where linked departments have all-to-all contact between their members. Unlike the other products, it is not commutative. Both graphs must be directed or both undirected. Every product edge comes from one factor edge, whose weight and attributes it keeps. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The graph substituted for each node. Neither graph is modified. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with `n * m` nodes, numbered and labeled as in `cartesian_product()`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If one graph is directed and the other is not. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} An undirected simple product has $|E_G| m^2 + n |E_H|$ edges. Results match NetworkX's `lexicographic_product`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two linked departments, each a team of two colleagues: everyone across the link is connected, giving a complete graph on four nodes: ::: {#b029a91c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec departments = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["sales", "ops"]).add_edge("sales", "ops") team = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["lead", "rep"]).add_edge("lead", "rep") org = departments.lexicographic_product(team) org.count_edges(), org.is_isomorphic(ec.Graph().add_full_graph(4)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (6, True) ``` ::: ::: The order matters: with no edge inside each team, only the cross-team links remain: ::: {#3d8cc7d3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} solo = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["lead", "rep"]) departments.lexicographic_product(solo).count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 4 ``` ::: :::
